title: Investigation 01: Microsoft Security Alert
subject: URGENT: Unusual Sign-in Activity Detected
scenario: We detected an unusual sign-in attempt on your Microsoft 365 account. Review the activity immediately to prevent account restrictions.
email_note: The message claims to be from Microsoft Security.
options: Report the email as phishing because the sender domain is not Microsoft's official domain.
Click the link because the email mentions unusual sign-in activity.
Reply to the sender asking whether the alert is genuine.
Forward the email to colleagues to check whether they received it.
explanation: The sender uses a lookalike domain with a zero replacing the letter 'o'. Attackers imitate trusted brands and create urgency to make employees click malicious links. Report the message through the approved security reporting process.

title: Investigation 02: Identify the Legitimate Fuji Silvertech Email
sender_email: Compare Email A and Email B
subject: Company Password Maintenance Notification
scenario: You receive two emails that appear to come from Fuji Silvertech IT Support. Both discuss company password maintenance. One is legitimate, while the other is designed to steal employee credentials.

emails.label: EMAIL A
emails.subject: Scheduled Password Maintenance
emails.body:
Dear Employee,

The IT team will be conducting scheduled password maintenance this weekend.

No immediate action is required. If you need to update your password, please access the company portal using your usual bookmarked address.

For assistance, contact the IT Helpdesk through the approved internal support channel.

Regards,
IT Support Team

emails.label: EMAIL B
emails.subject: URGENT: Your Company Account Will Be Deactivated
emails.body:
Dear Employee,

Your Fuji Silvertech account will be deactivated today due to a security issue.

You must complete the account verification process immediately.

Enter your company password and MFA code using the link below to avoid account suspension.

Regards,
IT Support Team

email_note: Compare the sender addresses, domains, urgency, links and information requested.
options: Email A is legitimate and Email B is suspicious.
Email B is legitimate and Email A is suspicious.
Both emails are legitimate.
Both emails are phishing.
explanation: Email A uses the official company domain and directs employees to access the company portal through their usual bookmarked address. Email B uses an unverified lookalike domain, creates urgency and asks for a password and MFA code. Never provide credentials through an email link.

title: Investigation 03: The Shared Document Trap
subject: A colleague has shared a confidential document with you
scenario:
Hello,

A confidential document has been shared with you. You must open it within 30 minutes or your access will be permanently removed.

To view the document, sign in using your company email, password and MFA code.

If you have any questions, do not contact IT because this is an automated sharing process.

Regards,
Document Collaboration Team
email_note: The message contains an unexpected document-sharing request.
options: Open the document immediately because it mentions a colleague.
Enter your company credentials to prevent losing access.
Verify the document-sharing request through a trusted channel and report it if suspicious.
Forward the document to your personal email account.
explanation: Unexpected document-sharing messages should be verified through a trusted channel. External domains, artificial deadlines, credential requests and instructions not to contact IT are strong warning signs.

title: Investigation 04: Identify the Legitimate HR Salary Email
sender_email: Compare Email A and Email B
subject: Annual Salary Revision Notification
scenario: Two emails arrive announcing the annual salary revision. Both appear to come from Human Resources. One follows a normal company communication process, while the other attempts to collect sensitive employee information.

emails.label: EMAIL A
emails.subject: Annual Salary Revision Announcement
emails.body:
Dear Employee,

The annual salary revision process has been completed.

Employees will receive their individual revision letters through the approved HR communication channel.

No password, banking credentials or additional personal information is required through email.

For questions, please contact the HR department using the official internal contact details.

Regards,
Human Resources Team

emails.label: EMAIL B
emails.subject: URGENT: Annual Salery Revision - Action Required
emails.body:
Dear Employee,

Your annual salery revision has been approved. Please compleate your employee information update immediately.

Use the link below to confirm your revised salary.

You must provide your bank account details and current company password to receive your revised salary.

Regards,
Human Resources

email_note: Compare the sender domain, spelling, requested information and communication process.
options: Email A is legitimate and Email B is suspicious.
Email B is legitimate and Email A is suspicious.
Both emails are legitimate.
Both emails are phishing.
explanation: Email A uses the official company domain and directs employees to the approved HR communication channel. Email B uses an unverified domain, contains spelling mistakes and requests banking details and a company password. HR should never request company passwords through email.

title: Investigation 05: Project Coordination Update
subject: Updated Project Timeline and Meeting Notes
scenario:
Hello Team,

Please find the updated project timeline and meeting notes attached. The revised milestones are highlighted for your review.

Please share any feedback during our scheduled project meeting.

Regards,
Project Coordination Team
email_note: This message was received from an internal company address.
options: Report it as phishing because all attachments are unsafe.
Treat it as potentially legitimate, verify the sender and attachment context, and review it using normal company procedures.
Forward the attachment to your personal email for easier access.
Reply with your company password to confirm receipt.
explanation: The email uses the company domain and describes a plausible work-related update. However, employees should still verify unexpected attachments and follow normal company security procedures rather than assuming every internal email is safe.

title: Investigation 06: Advanced Security Policy Update
subject: Mandatory Security Policy Review
scenario:
Dear Employee,

The Information Security Team has published an updated security policy. Please review the document through the company portal.

The message includes a link to an external file-sharing service that requests your company credentials before displaying the policy.

Regards,
Information Security Team
email_note: The sender address appears internal, but the link points to an external website.
options: Trust the email because the sender address belongs to the company.
Enter your credentials because the policy review is mandatory.
Do not enter credentials. Verify the external link with the Information Security Team through an approved channel.
Forward the link to your team and ask them to test it.
explanation: A legitimate-looking sender address does not guarantee that every link in a message is safe. The external file-sharing page requests company credentials. Verify the destination using an approved company portal or contact the security team directly.

title: Investigation 07: HR Benefits Announcement
subject: New Employee Benefits Enrollment
scenario:
Hello Team,

The annual employee benefits enrollment period is approaching. An unexpected message in a group chat asks employees to complete a benefits form using an unfamiliar external website and submit personal details immediately.

What should you do?
email_note: The message combines a genuine workplace topic with an unfamiliar external form.
options: Submit your details because benefits enrollment is important.
Share the form in your team group so everyone can complete it.
Verify the enrollment announcement with HR using an approved company channel before submitting any information.
Enter your personal details but leave the password field blank.
explanation: Attackers often use genuine workplace topics such as benefits enrollment to make fraudulent requests seem believable. Verify the announcement directly with HR and use only approved company systems.

title: Investigation 08: Identify the Legitimate Google Storage Email
sender_email: Compare Email A and Email B
subject: Google Storage Usage Notification
scenario: You receive two storage notifications. Both claim that your cloud storage requires attention. Compare the sender, message and requested action to identify the legitimate notification.

emails.label: EMAIL A
emails.subject: Google Account Storage Usage Update
emails.body:
Hello,

This is a notification about the storage usage associated with your Google Account.

You can review your current storage usage by navigating directly to your Google Account or Google One settings.

If you need additional storage, review the available options through the official Google website.

Google Workspace Support

emails.label: EMAIL B
emails.subject: URGENT: Your Google Storage Is Almost Full
emails.body:
Dear User,

Your cloud storage is almost full. Immediate action is requird to prevent your files from being deleted.

You are recieving this notification because your storage limit has been exceeded.

Upgrade or verify your storage immediately using the link below.

Your files will be removed immediatly unless you enter your account password and payment details.

Google Workspace Support

email_note: Compare the sender domain, spelling mistakes, urgency and destination links.
options: Email A is legitimate and Email B is suspicious.
Email B is legitimate and Email A is suspicious.
Both emails are legitimate.
Both emails are phishing.
explanation: Email A directs the employee to Google's official website to review storage usage. Email B uses an unverified lookalike domain, contains spelling mistakes, threatens immediate deletion and requests a password and payment details. Never provide credentials or payment details through an unverified email link.

title: Investigation 09: Vendor Payment Confirmation
subject: Invoice Processing Confirmation - INV-2048
scenario:
Hello,

This is a confirmation that invoice INV-2048 has been received for processing. The payment details will be reviewed according to the standard approval workflow.

No additional credentials or payment information are required through email.

Regards,
Accounts Payable Team
email_note: The message does not request credentials or ask the employee to change payment details.
options: Treat it as potentially legitimate, and verify the invoice through the normal finance workflow if needed.
Send your banking password to Accounts Payable to speed up processing.
Click any payment link received in a follow-up message without checking it.
Forward the confirmation to an external personal email account.
explanation: The message describes a routine invoice-processing confirmation and does not request credentials or unusual action. Continue to follow the normal finance approval process and verify any unexpected changes to payment instructions.

title: Investigation 10: Executive Impersonation
subject: Confidential: Urgent Gift Card Purchase
scenario:
I am currently in an important meeting and cannot take calls. I need you to purchase gift cards immediately and send me the redemption codes. Keep this request confidential and do not discuss it with anyone else.

I will explain everything later.

Regards,
CEO
email_note: The sender claims to be a senior executive and requests an urgent confidential transaction.
options: Purchase the gift cards immediately because the request comes from the CEO.
Reply with the gift card codes and wait for confirmation.
Verify the request using a known company contact method and report the suspicious message.
Ask a colleague to purchase the gift cards instead.
explanation: This is a common business email compromise technique. Attackers impersonate executives, create urgency, request secrecy and ask employees to make unusual payments. Always verify financial requests through a separate trusted communication channel.
